asOf: 2025 (NCSL 2025 page and 2025 Oklahoma comparison for AK, AL, AR, AZ, CA, CO; NCSL 2023 table for the rest)
about: Daily expense allowance each legislature pays its members during session, in cents; a place with no per diem is listed with basis none and zero.

ncsl2023.title: NCSL 2023 Legislative Compensation and Travel Expense Allowances

okla2025.title: Oklahoma 2025 legislative pay comparison with neighboring states

US-AK.note: Flat daily rate paid automatically on eligible days; taxable for some members.

US-AL.note: Tiered by distance from home base: nothing under 6 hours away, $34 for 12+ hours with no overnight, $85 for one night, $100 a day for two or more nights; paid without receipts.

US-AR.note: $166 a day for members living more than 50 miles from the Capitol, $59 for those within 50 miles.

US-AS.note: Members get a per diem only with an approved travel authorization, at the federal rate, vouchered; salary is $25,000 a year.
US-AS.estimatedFrom: US federal (GSA) per diem order of magnitude for a single travel day, since the territory publishes no session-day figure

US-AZ.note: Members outside Maricopa County get 100% of the federal per diem for Maricopa County for the first 120 days, half after; Maricopa County residents get $35. Set yearly.

US-CA.note: Flat daily rate paid automatically; tax exempt.

US-CO.note: $237 a day for members living more than 50 miles from the Capitol, $45 within 50 miles; vouchered; tied to the federal rate from 2025.

US-CT.note: No per diem; members get a $40,000 annual salary and mileage.

US-DC.note: Council members get no per diem; salary is $154,438 and out-of-town mileage is reimbursed.

US-DE.note: No per diem; members get $49,202 a year and mileage.

US-FL.note: Rates are set by the Speaker and Senate President; amounts are not published. Salary is $18,000 a year.
US-FL.estimatedFrom: Florida statute 112.061 in-state travel allowance range and the Tallahassee federal per diem; no published legislative rate

US-GA.note: Flat daily rate paid automatically on eligible days.

US-GU.note: No published session per diem; senators receive a $54,080 annual salary (2019 data) and are paid travel allowances only on official off-island travel.
US-GU.estimatedFrom: NCSL lists no data for Guam; based on the territory paying an annual salary and travel-only allowances

US-HI.note: Paid to members from outside Oahu only; tax exempt.

US-IA.note: $175 a day, or $131.25 for members living in Polk County; paid automatically.

US-ID.note: $221 a day for members more than 50 miles from the Capitol, $74 within 50 miles; tied to federal rates.

US-IN.note: Vouchered daily rate tied to the federal rate; members may also claim it outside session.

US-KS.note: Paid automatically on session days, on top of a $86.66 daily salary.

US-KY.note: $203.28 a day for members sworn in after 2023 ($188.22 before); paid automatically.

US-LA.note: Changes with the federal rate each Oct 1.

US-MA.note: No per diem; members get an annual expense allowance of $15,000 (within 50 miles) or $20,000 (beyond).

US-MD.note: Lodging $108 plus meals $63 a day, reimbursed with receipts.

US-ME.note: $70 a day lodging (or round-trip mileage instead) plus $50 meals, vouchered.

US-MI.note: No per diem; members get a $10,800 yearly expense allowance, vouchered.

US-MN.note: House members get $66 a day and senators $86; the midpoint is used for a combined legislature.
US-MN.estimatedFrom: Average of the $66 House and $86 Senate rates

US-MP.note: Members do not receive a per diem; salary is $32,000 a year (2023 NCSL).

US-MS.note: Tied to the federal rate; House members must be present at roll call.

US-MT.note: Paid automatically on top of a $104.86 daily salary.

US-NE.note: $151 a day for members more than 50 miles from the Capitol, $55 within 50 miles; tied to federal rates.

US-NH.note: No per diem; the annual salary is $100 and members can claim mileage.

US-NJ.note: No per diem; members get $49,000 a year and no mileage.

US-NM.note: Unsalaried legislature; vouchered daily allowance (2023 figure).

US-NV.note: Set by NRS 218A.630 at a federal-linked rate; the amount is not published in the NCSL table. Salary is $130 per session day.
US-NV.estimatedFrom: Carson City federal (GSA) lodging plus meals, since the statute ties the allowance to the federal rate

US-NY.note: Members receive a per diem under Senate and Assembly guidelines; NCSL lists no amount.
US-NY.estimatedFrom: Albany federal (GSA) per diem order of magnitude; no published legislative rate

US-OH.note: No per diem; members get $69,876 a year and mileage if they live outside Franklin County.

US-PR.note: NCSL lists no data for Puerto Rico; legislators receive session allowances (dietas) set by law.
US-PR.estimatedFrom: Order of magnitude of a Commonwealth legislative session-day allowance; no published figure found

US-RI.note: No per diem; members get $17,626.63 a year and mileage.

US-SC.note: Vouchered; tax exempt for some members.

US-SD.note: Paid to members who live more than 50 miles from the Capitol; tax exempt.

US-TN.note: $313 a day for members living 50 or more miles from the Capitol, $79 within 50 miles.

US-UT.note: Paid on receipts: breakfast up to $13, lunch $15, dinner $26, plus lodging and mileage; salary is $293.55 per legislative day.
US-UT.estimatedFrom: Meal caps only; lodging is reimbursed on top at actual cost

US-VI.note: Members do not receive a per diem; salary is $85,000 a year.

US-VT.note: Meals $69 a day plus lodging $134 a night, reimbursed with receipts.

US-WI.note: House overnight rate; $77.85 non-overnight. Senate is up to $140 a day (Dane County half).

US-WV.note: $175 a day for members who do not commute daily, $75 for those who do.

US-WY.note: Vouchered; paid on top of a $150 daily salary.
